titleStmt.title: Memorandum Regarding the Conduct of Base Negotiations With Spain

head.hi: Memorandum Regarding the Conduct of Base Negotiations With Spain

div.p: The following course of action is recommended for the negotiation with the Spanish Government of the military operating facilities required in Spain.

Admiral Sherman or another high-ranking officer should accompany the Ambassador when the negotiations are opened. This would involve discussions with General Franco to follow up his assurance to the Ambassador that base facilities in Spanish territory would be available to the U.S. and his agreement in principle of June 27 to “conversations of a defensive military character.” Subsequent discussions with high Spanish military authorities would probably then take place.

Since a high-ranking officer would undoubtedly be unable to remain to carry out the entire negotiations, these initial talks should prepare the way for a small group from Defense to continue the negotiations. As in the case of the current Azores negotiations with the Portuguese Government, this group would be under the general direction of the Ambassador and would be assisted, as required, by the Service Attachés and by other members of the Embassy staff. It should consist of a high-ranking officer from both the Air Force and the Navy; these Departments will probably each wish to send a representative from their legal staffs and the office of the Secretary of Defense may also wish to be represented.

The Ambassador should be instructed in advance to inform Franco that it is planned to send a high-ranking officer to Spain to initiate negotiations for air and naval base facilities in Spain. He
should also be instructed to ask Franco to receive him and this officer.

From what is known of the Ambassador’s opinion on this subject, he would welcome both Admiral Sherman’s visit and the assistance of other officers in the technical military and legal aspects which these negotiations will involve.

The agreement itself can be set up in the same general pattern we are using in other cases. This would include a main government-to-government agreement with one or more annexes covering the more technical military, jurisdictional and other matters which are not covered in the government agreement. The details on this can be worked out with the Air Force and Navy.

note.p: For information on this subject, see Document 352.

President Truman approved this memorandum and the dispatch of Admiral Sherman to Spain at the Cabinet meeting on July 6. (Memorandum dated July 6 and letter from Secretary Acheson to Secretary Marshall, dated July 10, S/S–NSC files, lot 63D351, NSC 72 files)
